reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 concerns an amorphous film and thermal shock, not nanocrystalline refinement or dynamic self-healing. E2 is a generic claim about boron doping without specific data on passive films or strain accommodation. E3 only demonstrates static corrosion resistance of a CoCrFeNiMo coating, with no tribocorrosion, microstructural refinement, or self-healing evidence.
premises: Refined (nanocrystalline) subsurface microstructure promotes formation of a dense, self-healing passive film in HEAs
The passive film is formed from elements like Mo and Cr and inhibits corrosion
The refined microstructure accommodates strain during sliding, limiting crack initiation and abrasive wear
The passive film acts as a solid lubricant to mitigate wear
A synergistic coupling exists between wear resistance and corrosion protection via this film
